data.title: Sitryx reports phase 1b data for SYX-5219
data.description:
Sitryx Therapeutics has announced positive topline phase 1b results for SYX-5219, a first-in-class oral PKM2 modulator being developed for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.

The findings provide the first clinical evidence that targeting PKM2 to modulate immune cell metabolism can deliver meaningful benefit for patients with atopic dermatitis. SYX-5219 was safe and well tolerated over the six-week treatment period, with pharmacokinetic and target engagement findings consistent with earlier healthy volunteer studies.

Iain Kilty said: “These positive results are an exciting milestone for Sitryx and a testament to the excellent execution by our team and clinical partners.”

He added: “We have provided the first human validation for a differentiated oral therapy, demonstrating activity across multiple clinical endpoints and biomarkers in patients with atopic dermatitis.”

The randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial enrolled 35 adults across sites in the United States and Europe. Patients received SYX-5219 or placebo for six weeks, followed by a 14-day off-treatment period. Differences from placebo were observed from Day 8, increasing throughout the dosing period. SYX-5219 met exploratory efficacy targets for skin disease severity, measured by EASI, and itch, measured by PP-NRS.

At six weeks, the placebo-adjusted change in total EASI score was approximately 28%, while the placebo-adjusted difference in PP-NRS itch score was around 48%. An increasing number of patients achieved at least a one-point improvement in vIGA, supported by reductions in several atopic dermatitis biomarkers.

Biomarker decreases included CCL-17/TARC and CCL-11/eotaxin, which significantly correlated with improvements in disease activity. Additional exploratory findings, including reductions in IL-13 and IgE, support investigation of PKM2 modulation in asthma and other inflammatory diseases.

data.title: Libtayo dosing backed by CHMP
data.description:
The CHMP has issued a positive opinion recommending approval of an alternative dosing schedule for Libtayo (cemiplimab) across all approved indications.

The opinion supports reducing dosing frequency from every three weeks to every six weeks after the first 12 weeks of treatment. It also recommends an optional reduction of infusion time for the 350 mg dose to 15 to 30 minutes, provided the first dose over 30 minutes was well tolerated.

A spokesperson for Regeneron said: “The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use has adopted a positive opinion recommending the approval of an alternative dosing schedule for Libtayo across all approved indications.”

They added: “The positive CHMP opinion is supported by comprehensive pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling and simulation data, integrated with clinical safety and efficacy data from Libtayo’s clinical development program.”

The recommendation supports a higher-dose 700 mg infusion every six weeks following an initial 12-week regimen of 350 mg every three weeks.

It also allows a shorter infusion option for patients continuing on the 350 mg schedule. The European Commission is expected to make a final decision in the coming months, which would enable the updated regimen to be applied across all six approved indications.

The 700 mg six-week option is already approved in the US for use after 12 weeks as an adjuvant treatment for adults with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma at high risk of recurrence. Across other indications, the existing 350 mg three-week regimen remains in place.

Libtayo is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1 and has been approved in more than 30 countries for certain adult patients with advanced BCC, CSCC, NSCLC and cervical cancer.

It is also being investigated in trials as a monotherapy and in combination approaches for other solid tumours, although these potential uses remain investigational and unapproved.

data.title: Sanofi breaks ground on new insulin facility
data.description:
Sanofi has broken ground on a new state-of-the-art insulin manufacturing facility at its BioCampus in Frankfurt, Germany.

The development will introduce a new generation of insulin production to one of the company’s largest integrated research and manufacturing sites and strengthen long-term supply for millions of people living with diabetes worldwide.

Prime Minister of the State of Hesse Boris Rhein and Mayor of Frankfurt Mike Josef joined Belén Garijo, Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi, Brendan O’Callaghan, Sanofi Executive Vice President, Manufacturing & Supply and Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Sanofi in Germany, and Madeleine Roach, Country President of Sanofi in Germany, at the groundbreaking ceremony.

Belén Garijo explained: “Millions of people around the world rely on insulin every day, and our commitment to them is for the long term. With this new facility, we are investing in the next generation of insulin manufacturing in Europe, building on more than a century of expertise and a strong industrial footprint in Frankfurt.”

She added: “Maintaining the right conditions for investment and innovation will be essential to Europe’s future competitiveness.”

The new facility will be built on a 36,000-square-meter footprint at the BioCampus, equivalent to approximately five football fields. It will meet high standards of quality and automation and use advanced digital technologies and artificial intelligence across manufacturing and quality processes.

Full production of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredient is planned for 2032 once the facility is fully licensed. It will be among the largest and most advanced insulin manufacturing facilities in Europe and a key part of Sanofi’s global insulin supply network.

More than 500 million people worldwide live with diabetes, with numbers expected to rise to over 800 million by 2050. Sanofi currently supplies insulin to approximately 15 million people in more than 100 countries each year.

The new Frankfurt facility reflects the company’s long-term commitment to people who rely on insulin and will help ensure its manufacturing network can serve patients for decades to come.

data.title: CHMP backs TALVEY plus daratumumab for earlier myeloma use
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson has announced that the CHMP recommends approval of an indication extension for TALVEY (talquetamab) plus daratumumab, with or without pomalidomide, for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior therapy.

If approved, the combination would be the only GPRC5D-targeting bispecific antibody therapy available as early as second line.

Ester in ’t Groen said: “MonumenTAL-3 demonstrated significant improvements in progression-free survival, overall survival, response rates and depth of response with the combination of talquetamab and daratumumab.”

She added: “For patients facing their first relapse, this combination has the potential to provide deep responses and keep their disease under control for longer at a critical point in their treatment journey.”

Yusri Elsayed explained: “At Johnson & Johnson, our strategy is grounded in pursuing differentiated immunotherapy approaches earlier in the disease course to address diverse patient characteristics and the evolving complexity of multiple myeloma.”

He added: “By simultaneously targeting GPRC5D and CD38, our goal is to deliver deeper and longer lasting responses for patients.”

The phase 3 MonumenTAL-3 study evaluated talquetamab plus daratumumab (Tal-D) or Tal-D and pomalidomide (Tal-DP) compared to daratumumab plus pomalidomide and dexamethasone. At a median follow-up of 24.6 months, Tal-DP achieved progression-free survival of 81.3% and Tal-D achieved 77.6%. Overall survival at 24 months reached 89.2% for Tal-DP and 87.9% for Tal-D.

Safety findings were consistent with known profiles of each monotherapy. Rates of grade 3/4 infections were lowest with Tal-D at 29.2%, followed by Tal-DP at 37.7% and DPd at 42.2%. Treatment discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in 10.5% of Tal-DP, 8.0% of Tal-D and 6.7% of DPd patients.

data.title: CHMP backs RASONQUE for metastatic pancreatic cancer
data.description:
Revolution Medicines has received a positive CHMP opinion recommending marketing authorisation for RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) as a once-daily oral monotherapy for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy.

If approved by the EC, it would become the first broad RAS-targeted treatment option available in the EU for this patient group.

Mark A. Goldsmith said: “Today’s positive CHMP opinion marks a major step toward making RASONQUE available to eligible adults with metastatic pancreatic cancer in the European Union.”

He added: “RASONQUE is an oral medicine designed to address RAS, the key driver of pancreatic cancer, and unprecedented results from the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial demonstrated its potential to benefit patients with this devastating disease.”

The phase 3 RASolute 302 trial compared RASONQUE with investigator’s choice of cytotoxic chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic PDAC. The study met all primary and key secondary endpoints in both the RAS G12 mutant population and the overall intent-to-treat population.

In the intent-to-treat population, RASONQUE reduced the risk of death by 60% compared with chemotherapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.40. Median overall survival reached 13.2 months with RASONQUE versus 6.7 months for chemotherapy.

RASONQUE also delivered significant improvements in progression-free survival, with a hazard ratio of 0.49. Median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with RASONQUE compared to 3.6 months with chemotherapy. A subsequent ad hoc analysis showed median overall survival of 12.4 months with RASONQUE versus 6.7 months for chemotherapy, consistent with the primary analysis.

The most common adverse reactions included diarrhea, dermatitis acneiform, stomatitis, nausea, vomiting and fatigue. Once granted, the centralized EC authorisation will apply across all EU member states and EEA countries Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein.

data.title: ViiV and Axmed expand access to HIV medicines
data.description:
ViiV Healthcare has signed an agreement appointing Axmed as a non-exclusive distributor to support procurement and supply of its HIV medicines in more than 50 middle-income countries, subject to local regulatory requirements.

The partnership aims to provide a simpler route to access more choice in HIV care and strengthen national HIV responses. Most new HIV cases occur in low- and middle-income countries, where access challenges remain significant.

Axmed operates a technology-enabled business-to-business platform connecting healthcare procurers with suppliers to improve access to medicines. Through its digital tools, governments and healthcare institutions can lower procurement costs and streamline logistics, helping health systems reach more people with available resources. Middle-income countries often face distinct barriers and may not qualify for certain lower-income access mechanisms, underscoring the need for new models to expand access.

Deborah Waterhouse said: “This agreement underlines ViiV Healthcare’s leadership in the global HIV response and our deep understanding of the realities in middle-income countries.”

She added: “Shaped by listening closely to communities and governments, this announcement is an important step in supporting them to access more choice in HIV care, strengthen health systems and accelerate progress towards our shared goal of ending the HIV epidemic.”

Emmanuel Akpakwu said: “The promise of medical innovation is only fulfilled when it reaches the people who need it. Technology gives us an extraordinary opportunity to reimagine how that happens, connecting fragmented markets, unlocking more affordable procurement and streamlining access to vital medicines.”

He added: “Through this agreement with ViiV Healthcare, we are working towards a future where more people can benefit from advances in HIV care, regardless of where they live.”

Both organisations share a commitment to improving access in countries where health systems face challenges. As the number of people living with HIV continues to rise, the agreement supports ViiV Healthcare’s ambition to broaden access through partnerships, programmes and technologies.

data.title: RougeTx launches with $58 million series A financing for HHT therapy
data.description:
RougeTx has launched with a $58 million series A financing to advance RTX‑001, a potential once‑daily oral treatment designed to restore blood vessel stability in HHT. The round was co‑led by BGV, Angelini Ventures and Kurma Partners, with participation from Epidarex Capital, Vesalius Biocapital Partners, ROM Utrecht Region, p53 Invest and Kerna Ventures.

The funding will support RTX‑001 as it progresses toward first‑in‑human development. HHT is the second most common inherited bleeding disorder, caused by abnormal blood vessel formation known as AVMs. These can lead to recurrent nose and gastrointestinal bleeding, iron deficiency, chronic anemia and serious complications affecting major organs. There are currently no approved therapies for HHT.

Andrew Lightfoot, Chief Executive Officer at RougeTx, said: “RTX-001 is designed to stabilize fragile blood vessels by restoring pericyte attachment. The data we have generated for RTX-001 gives us a strong foundation as we move toward the clinic. This financing also allows us to explore where the same biology may impact other vascular diseases.”

Franck Lebrin, Co‑Founder and Scientific Advisor at RougeTx, remarked: “RougeTx represents the culmination of more than 20 years of research, initially at Inserm and over the past decade in my laboratory at Leiden University Medical Center. I am excited by the opportunity to bring a novel treatment to the HHT community.”

Sandra Glucksmann, Executive Chair at RougeTx, noted: “For too long, people living with HHT have faced a serious, lifelong disease with no approved treatment options. RougeTx was founded with a commitment to this community and a belief that advances in vascular biology can finally make a meaningful difference for patients and families. We are grateful to our investors for their support and shared commitment to our mission.”

RougeTx’s periSCOPE platform is designed to expand the pipeline beyond HHT, identifying new treatment opportunities in diseases driven by vascular instability and supporting development of small‑molecule therapies based on shared underlying biology.

data.title: Lundbeck presents phase 1b data for Lu AF28996 in advanced Parkinson’s disease
data.description:
Lundbeck has reported results from an open‑label phase 1b trial evaluating Lu AF28996, an investigational oral prodrug of a D1‑like/D2‑like dopamine receptor agonist, in people with advanced Parkinson’s disease whose motor symptoms remained sub‑optimally controlled despite optimized non‑invasive treatment. The findings are being presented at MDS 2026 in Seoul.

Parkinson’s disease involves progressive degeneration of dopamine‑producing neurons. Many people develop motor complications over time, including fluctuations between Good ON‑time and OFF‑time, and treatment‑related dyskinesia. Existing options for advanced disease often require invasive procedures or continuous drug delivery, highlighting the need for effective non‑invasive approaches.

Tarek Samad, Executive Vice President and Head of Research & Development at Lundbeck, said: “Many people with advanced Parkinson’s disease continue to experience motor fluctuations and dyskinesia that can significantly affect daily life. We are encouraged by the phase Ib results with Lu AF28996, including the improvements observed alongside substantial reductions in levodopa dose. With the DARE2 phase II trial now underway, we are taking the next step in evaluating its potential in a larger, randomized and controlled study.”

In part B of the trial, 34 participants received Lu AF28996 twice daily for six weeks, with 25 continuing for an optional 12‑week extension. Most treatment‑emergent adverse events were mild, with no unexpected safety signals. The most common events were nausea, dizziness and fall.

At baseline, participants experienced a mean of 9.5 hours of Good ON‑time, 4.7 hours of OFF‑time and 1.8 hours of ON‑time with troublesome dyskinesia. At Weeks 6 and 18, Good ON‑time increased by 3.6 and 3.4 hours, OFF‑time decreased by 2.3 and 2.0 hours, and ON‑time with troublesome dyskinesia decreased by 1.2 and 1.4 hours. Dyskinesia severity, measured by UDysRS, improved by 8.5 points at Week 6 and 14.5 points at Week 18. Mean daily levodopa dose fell by 53.4% at Week 6 and 29.2% at Week 18.

Among participants with at least one hour per day of troublesome dyskinesia at baseline, ON‑time with troublesome dyskinesia decreased by 2.3 hours at Week 6 and 2.8 hours at Week 18. The exploratory trial involved a limited number of participants and no placebo or active comparator.

DARE2, a phase 2 randomised, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial, is now underway and will evaluate Lu AF28996 in approximately 150 adults. The primary endpoint is change from baseline to Week 19 in daily Good ON‑time. Recruitment has begun in the US, with additional sites planned across Europe and Japan.

Lu AF28996 is not approved by the FDA or any other regulatory agency, and its efficacy and safety have not been established.

data.title: Osivax reports phase 2b data for OVX836
data.description:
Osivax has reported phase 2b results for OVX836 and outlined the next stage of development for its next-generation seasonal influenza vaccine strategy.

The study evaluated OVX836 in 2,850 healthy adults in Europe and delivered what the company describes as the first consistent efficacy signal for a monovalent nucleoprotein-based influenza vaccine across both major influenza A subtypes.

The trial did not meet its pre-specified primary endpoint of 50% vaccine efficacy, with a point estimate of 24% that was not statistically significant.

Secondary endpoints showed emerging efficacy signals, including 28% for CDC-defined influenza-like illness, 27% for A/H3 and 25% for A/H1N1pdm09. OVX836 also demonstrated a favourable safety profile and induced robust NP-specific antibody and T-cell responses. Osivax said these findings support advancing OVX836 in combination with traditional seasonal influenza vaccines to provide a complementary layer of protection.

Dr Nicola Groth said: “Large efficacy studies are designed not only to evaluate clinical benefit, but also to deepen our understanding of novel immune mechanisms under real-world conditions.”

She added: “While the study did not meet its primary endpoint, the consistency of the efficacy signal across influenza A subtypes, together with the observed immunogenicity and favourable safety profile, reinforces our confidence that nucleoprotein-targeted immunity can provide a complementary mechanism of protection alongside conventional seasonal influenza vaccines.”

Alexandre Le Vert said: “These results provide a clear direction for the future development of OVX836. Rather than replacing existing seasonal influenza vaccines, we believe the greatest opportunity lies in complementing them.”

He added: “By combining strain-specific antibody protection with the broad cellular immunity induced by OVX836, we aim to develop next-generation influenza vaccines capable of delivering broader and more durable protection against seasonal influenza.”

Osivax has secured collaborations with GC Biopharma and a second undisclosed pharmaceutical partner to support development of single-injection combination candidates. The first phase 1/2 combination study is expected in Q4 2027.

data.title: Merz completes phase 3 recruitment for XEOMIN
data.description:
Merz Therapeutics has completed patient recruitment in two global phase 3 trials evaluating XEOMIN (incobotulinumtoxinA) for the prevention of episodic and chronic migraine.

Recruitment finished six months ahead of schedule, with around 1800 adults enrolled across 109 study sites in North America and Europe. Migraine affects an estimated 1.1 billion people worldwide and represents a significant burden for patients, society and healthcare systems.

Both MINT-E and MINT-C are assessing the change in monthly migraine days from baseline to Month 6 as the primary endpoint.

Secondary endpoints include changes in monthly headache days, acute medication days and migraine frequency during two-week periods at the end of each injection cycle. The studies aim to determine whether XEOMIN can offer a preventive treatment option for adults with episodic or chronic migraine.

Dr Stefan Albrecht said: “Achieving patient recruitment for both MINT-C and MINT-E six months ahead of plan is an important milestone for our XEOMIN migraine prevention program. I am proud of what our teams, investigators and patients have achieved together.”

He added: “With recruitment now complete, our focus is on the main study period and subsequent analysis of the data. These results will guide our next clinical and regulatory decisions as we evaluate XEOMIN for the preventive treatment of chronic and episodic migraine.”
